chunks.arabic_text: مُعَلَّى بْنُ خُنَيْسٍ، مَوْلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ (عليه السلام). كَانَ أَوَّلُ أَمْرِهِ مُغَيِّرِيًّا، ثُمَّ دَعَا إِلَى مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ، وَفِي هَذِهِ الظَّنَّةِ أَخَذَهُ دَاوُدُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ فَقَتَلَهُ. وَالْغُلَاةُ يُضِيفُونَ إِلَيْهِ كَثِيرًا. وَلَا أَرَى الِاعْتِمَادَ عَلَى شَيْءٍ مِنْ حَدِيثِهِ.

translations.en: Muʿallā ibn Khunays, the client of Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him). The beginning of his affair was variable, then he called towards Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdillāh ibn al-Ḥasan, and in this supposition Dāwūd ibn ʿAlī took him and killed him. The ghulāt attached much to him. I do not regard anything of his ḥadīth to be credible.

en.summary: Muʿallā ibn Khunays, a prominent companion of the Imams, is presented here as a figure of nuanced reliability; while the Ghulāt (extremists) heavily attributed traditions to him, the author cautions against uncritical acceptance due to his shifting political allegiances and eventual martyrdom under the Umayyads. This entry highlights the critical methodology of hadith scholars in distinguishing between the spiritual status of a companion and the technical accuracy of his narrations, particularly in the context of the transition from the Umayyad to the Abbasid era.
en.seo_question: Who is Muʿallā ibn Khunays and why is he considered weak in hadith sciences?

key_terms.مَوْلَى: Client/mawla (a freed slave or non-Arab companion)
key_terms.مُغَيِّرِيًّا: Variable/fluctuating (referring to his changing political/religious stance)
key_terms.الظَّنَّةِ: Supposition/opinion (referring to the political context of his capture)
key_terms.الْغُلَاةُ: The Ghulāt (extremist sects who attributed divine qualities to Imams)
